name: The Binding
summary: In the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Forsaken warlocks seek to summon, conquer, and permanently command a voidwalker. Carendin Halgar oversees the rite that grants them this power.

sections.title: A Rite of Subjugation
sections.body: Forsaken warlocks must prove they can master a voidwalker before they may summon one. Unlike minor imps, which dark magic easily draws into pacts, creatures of the Void despise reality and possess formidable physical might. In the Magic Quarter, mentor Carendin Halgar provides the mystic runes required to tear a voidwalker from the Nether into the physical realm.

sections.title: Within the Circle
sections.body: Beneath Carendin Halgar's dais, a glowing summoning circle is etched into the floor. When the runes are activated, an unbound voidwalker appears in fury. You cannot subdue it through diplomacy; you must break it with arcane force and raw will. Only after the creature is thoroughly crushed does Carendin reveal the true summoning formula, which binds its essence to you indefinitely.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this ritual?
aliases: what does the binding quest do
faq.answer: The rite tests whether you can overpower a creature of the Void. Defeating an unbound voidwalker proves your will is strong enough to control it, and Carendin Halgar then teaches you the permanent summoning spell.

faq.q: Where does the summoning take place?
faq.answer: The summoning takes place in the purple circle etched into the floor beneath Carendin Halgar's platform in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity.
Carendin Halgar is the primary warlock trainer in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. He oversees instruction and dark initiations for newly raised Forsaken practitioners.

faq.q: Do warlocks need to defeat every demon they want to summon?
faq.answer: Warlocks must establish authority over powerful extradimensional beings before commanding them. Smaller entities like imps are bound by simple contracts and rituals, while voidwalkers require physical and magical dominance before they submit to servitude.

faq.q: What happens if a warlock fails to subdue the voidwalker?
aliases: what if i fail the binding
faq.answer: An unbound voidwalker relentlessly batters anyone nearby. Halgar warns that failing to meet his expectations is nothing compared to the danger of being torn apart by the untamed entity within the circle.

Voidwalkers are shadowy, extradimensional beings from the Void. They have immense physical resilience and an innate desire to extinguish living light and energy, making them ideal protective shields for practitioners of dark magic.

angles.text: As a warlock, this rite takes you from petty trickery with imps to domination over beings that can absorb immense physical punishment on the battlefield.
As one of the Forsaken, binding a creature of shadow extends your resilience and your lack of moral restraint regarding forbidden magic.
